The blank issue is now your "meta-issue"
---
The alternative is that you mark all of the issues as unplanned, then create a blank issue with a checklist, and then recreate all the sub tasks. 
Both will produce the same outcome but one should be much faster to do, if it works like that.
Can you handle this @rndquu ?

I think it doesn't read draft pulls right now. This will be fixed soon. Also strange it didn't warn at 3.5 days. @gentlementlegen

We should implement invariant testing for [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol). 
So collaborator who's going to take this issue should carefully study the  [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol) and think of the invariants that should be tested.
Invariants could be:
- user can not mint more Dollars in USD than provided collateral
- user can not redeem more collateral in USD than provided Dollar tokens
- https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/925#issuecomment-2128859442
Possible solutions for invariant testing (I would simply start with foundry since we're using it as a development framework + it also contains fuzz testing):
- https://book.getfoundry.sh/forge/invariant-testing
- https://github.com/crytic/echidna
- https://github.com/crytic/medusa
What should be done:
1. Impelent invariant tests for the  [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol) contract (you may create them in a separate test file like `UbiquityPoolFacet.invariant.t.sol` so we could distinguish unit, fuzz and invariant tests)
2. Setup testing CI this way:
a) On PR invariant tests should run with a small number of runs (so that we could merge PRs fast)
b) On merge to the `development` branch invariant tests should run with a great number of runs to test many cases (keep in mind that github action runnners can run for 6 hours)

yes
I don't really understand the question. We can't compile all of them in a single issue because each of those tasks is pretty time consuming.
I meant the same flow

I didn't forget about this task
We first need to remove mocks from the contracts because it doesn't make sense in fuzzing Dollar contracts which use mocks under the hood
I'll break down the "remove mocks" epic into subtasks soon

Invariant testing is a subpart of fuzzing tests which we already [run](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/development/.github/workflows/deep-fuzz.yml) on CI on push to the `development` branch. So I think for invariant tests we could use the same strategy (running on CI on push to the `development` branch).
Hey, sorry for a long response, I'll check it today
As far as I understand the `ubiquity-os` bot unassigned you because there was some period of inactivity

@alexandr-masl Overall this is a great job.
1. Pls fix minor issues in the comments
2. [Here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/pull/953#issuecomment-2327144003) you mention the `Users cannot redeem more collateral (in USD value) than the corresponding Dollar tokens` invariant test. Is it going to be implemented?
3. This issue also implies setting up CI. You may take [fuzzing CI](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/.github/workflows/deep-fuzz.yml) as an example.

Pls add this config to [foundry.toml](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/foundry.toml):
```toml
[profile.intense.invariant]
runs = 50000 # ~1 hour
```
Overall this is a good start. There're still too many reverts but it's something that we should work out in the next invariant tests iteration.

I know it's still a draft but it would be super cool to use different chainlink contracts that would return different values ([here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/66899068ea4604354f9f0becbd7e10855d974cbc/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol#L1190), [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/66899068ea4604354f9f0becbd7e10855d974cbc/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol#L1081) and [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/66899068ea4604354f9f0becbd7e10855d974cbc/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol#L1019)).

This line always reverts because `collateralRatio` [can't be greater](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol#L1068) than `1_000_000`. Pls refactor accordingly.

This handler method adds too much unnecessary reverts on collection redemption. We'd better:
1. Remove `setRedemptionDelay()` handler method
2. Set `redemptionDelayBlocks` to 0 (in order not to wait for passed blocks for collecting redemption) in [UbiquityPoolFacet.invariant.t.sol](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/dfff4f314386ef0ec4d0fb6091367623823480e0/packages/contracts/test/invariant/diamond/facets/UbiquityPoolFacet.invariant.t.sol)'s `setUp()`
This way we more or less simulate real user flow.
Shouldn't we use `vm.prank(user)` here?

Also may revert in some cases because collateral ratio can't be > `1_000_000`. Why do we even need to call `setCollateralRatio()` on setting chainlink related prices [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/dfff4f314386ef0ec4d0fb6091367623823480e0/packages/contracts/test/invariant/diamond/facets/PoolFacetHandler.sol#L157) and [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/dfff4f314386ef0ec4d0fb6091367623823480e0/packages/contracts/test/invariant/diamond/facets/PoolFacetHandler.sol#L178)?
Why do we `div(2)` here? What's the difference between `type(uint256).max.div(2)` and `type(uint256).max` in this particular case?

Invariant and fuzz CI workflows are kept in separate files because of github CI limit of running 6 hours per a single workflow run. If we keep invariant and fuzz tests in a single workflow file we're basically limiting ourselves to 3 hours of invariant and 3 hours of fuzzing execution time while with separate workflows we have 12 available execution hours (6 hours invariant + 6 hours fuzzing).
